semantics.raise: adds semaphore permits immediately, so queued spawns are admitted at once
semantics.lower: COOPERATIVE, never preemptive. Reclaims only permits free right now via Semaphore::forget_permits and retires the remainder as running sessions finish. Sessions already admitted run to completion - killing live model sessions to satisfy a settings change would destroy operator work and orphan processes, which HBR-QUIET-003 forbids.
semantics.return_value: the cap ACTUALLY in force, not the requested one, so a partially-applied reduction cannot be reported as complete
semantics.floor: clamped to 1; a zero cap would wedge the coordinator with no way to admit the spawn that would release a permit

ac_3_concurrency_control.route: GET/PUT /operator-chat/swarm/max-concurrent (api/operator_chat.rs), mounted there because the coordinator singleton is only reachable through OperatorChatLaunchService. PUT returns requested, max_concurrent (in force), fully_applied, and live_sessions so the operator surface can never display a limit the runtime is not honouring.

v5_remediation_ac3_convergence_2026_08_0.how_found: A delegated UserManual agent reported that PUT/GET /operator-chat/swarm/max-concurrent and SwarmCoordinator::set_max_concurrent had ZERO behavioural test coverage anywhere in the tree. Writing the missing tests exposed that the uncovered code was also WRONG.
v5_remediation_ac3_convergence_2026_08_0.defect: Lowering the cap did not converge. set_max_concurrent reclaimed only the permits free at request time via Semaphore::forget_permits, stored the partially-reduced value, and DISCARDED the remaining deficit - nothing remembered it. Permits handed back by finishing sessions returned to the semaphore and were recycled into new spawns, so the cap settled at whatever intermediate value happened to be reachable at request time and NEVER reached what the operator asked for. Worse, both the doc comment and the in-product UserManual asserted the opposite: that lowering 'retires the remainder as running sessions finish'. A control that reports success, is documented as converging, and silently does not is precisely the misleading control AC-3 exists to remove.
v5_remediation_ac3_convergence_2026_08_0.fix: Added Inner::desired_max_concurrent (the requested target) alongside effective_max_concurrent (the cap in force), plus Inner::reconcile_concurrency_cap, which drains the deficit as permits come free and is idempotent. It is called at EVERY point that can admit or report: before try_acquire_owned in the spawn admission path (so a permit freed after a lowering request cannot admit a spawn above the requested cap), in max_concurrent(), and at the end of set_max_concurrent. Raising still applies immediately AND cancels any pending lowering, so a newer operator instruction is never silently undone by an older one draining later. Lowering remains cooperative: running sessions are never killed (HBR-QUIET-003). Sub-1 requests are clamped to 1, because 0 would wedge the coordinator with no way to admit the spawn that would release a permit.
v5_remediation_ac3_convergence_2026_08_0.api_change: GET /operator-chat/swarm/max-concurrent now also returns `requested` and `fully_applied`, so a reader can distinguish 'the cap is 3' from 'the cap is 3 on its way down to 1'. PUT reports the CLAMPED target rather than echoing the raw body, so a request of 0 does not leave fully_applied false forever. Added SwarmCoordinator::requested_max_concurrent.
v5_remediation_ac3_convergence_2026_08_0.falsifiability_OBSERVED: Not argued - RUN. The fix was inverted (reconcile removed from max_concurrent() and from the spawn admission path, reproducing the old semantics exactly: set-time reclaim kept, later retirement removed) and the suite was rebuilt and re-executed. OBSERVED: 'test result: FAILED. 2 passed; 1 failed', with mt021_lowering... panicking at tests.rs:3769 -- assertion `left == right` failed: a permit freed after a lowering request must be retired, not reused / left: 2 / right: 1. That is the bug reproduced: the freed permit was recycled and the cap settled at 2 instead of converging to the requested 1. The inversion was then reverted and the suite re-run GREEN.
